first_missing_step.name: Non-low bounded-positive block occupation inequality
first_missing_step.inequality: Let A_q be the event that every pair total in block q lies in {1,...,B_0} and the block entry satisfies z>=eta, with no resonance restriction. Prove that there exist C<infinity and R_0 such that, for every sufficiently large accessible R=2J+epsilon and every actual coupled array (r,R,tau,K) satisfying the frozen constraints, E[exp(-lambda * sum_{q in Q_R} 1_{A_q}) | S_R=K and the exact first-passage data] <= C/R.
first_missing_step.why_strictly_narrower: Since C_q is a subset of A_q, sum_q 1_{A_q} >= sum_q 1_{C_q}, so exp(-lambda sum 1_{A_q}) <= exp(-lambda sum 1_{C_q}). Therefore the primary claim implies this inequality. It removes the short-orbit resonance arithmetic and isolates the first unresolved occupation problem.
first_missing_step.why_not_proved_by_displayed_reductions: The beta-binomial formula controls one sampled height, and exact composition counts control one prescribed word. Neither controls the joint lower tail across a growing disjoint grid. Endpoint conditioning creates dependence, low visits have positive probability, and no proved cycle/ballot identity resolves the affine threshold, rational ties, even-time sampling, and odd singleton conventions. Moreover, proving this inequality alone would still not establish the primary claim because resonant deletion remains.
